metadata.purpose: Manual, event-by-event crosswalk between the 9 post-1899 Ambraseys (2002) Table 1 events and data/eq_historical.json (ISC 1900-1997 + EMSC 1998-2026), per user instruction (2026-09-12) to resolve 'same event?' scientifically rather than via automated lat/lon/time-proximity dedup.
metadata.method: For each flagged Ambraseys event, data/eq_historical.json was searched within +-3 days and +-0.7 degrees of the Ambraseys coordinates; every candidate found is listed, and a manual same-event judgement is recorded with its rationale. No records were merged or removed from either source file -- this file only records the relationship.
metadata.epica_share_cet_note: data/epica_europe_historical.json (EPICA+SHARE-CET) is capped at year<=1899 and therefore cannot contain any of these 9 events by construction -- not queried.
metadata.display_policy: NOT YET DECIDED. Options to consider when the UI toggle is eventually built: (a) show both markers independently with a visual link (e.g. connecting line or shared canonical_event_id shown in both popups) when both layers are active; (b) show only the Ambraseys marker for pre-1970 events (better historical-context magnitude) and note the eq_historical.json record in its popup; (c) always show both, colored/labeled by source, and let the user judge. This decision is explicitly deferred to the index.html integration step and is NOT implemented in this data-only pass.

crosswalk.match_basis: Same calendar date; epicenters ~0.06 lat / ~0.18 lon apart (~18 km), consistent with early-20th-century macroseismic location uncertainty. Magnitude differs by 0.3 (Ms7.3 vs Mw7.6), plausible given different scales/eras but not identical -- treated as the same physical event (the well-known 1912 Ganos-Murefte earthquake) rather than a coincidence.

No candidate found in data/eq_historical.json within +-3 days / +-0.7 degrees of the Ambraseys coordinates. Not unexpected: ISC catalog coverage of Turkey for 1912 secondary/aftershock-sized events is sparse; this is a known large aftershock of the Aug 1912 Ganos-Murefte sequence per historical seismology literature, absent from the instrumental record used here.
crosswalk.note: Genuine gap in eq_historical.json, not an extraction error on either side.

crosswalk.match_basis: Identical date; epicenters ~0.1 lon apart (~8 km); magnitude essentially identical (6.8 vs 6.82, both reported as Ms) -- very likely the same underlying magnitude assessment.
Identical date; epicenters ~0.25 lon apart (~23 km, within expected location uncertainty for this era); magnitude very close (Ms7.1 vs Mw7.2).

Identical date; epicenters ~8 km apart; magnitude very close (Ms7.1 vs Mw7.2). Two additional smaller ISC events the same day (886606 Ms5.88, 886613 Ms5.66, ~09:36 and next-day 11:01) are NOT the same event -- likely a foreshock and an early aftershock, listed here for transparency but not linked to this canonical_event_id.
crosswalk.note: 886606 (Ms5.88, same-day foreshock) and 886613 (Ms5.66, next-day aftershock) found nearby but excluded from this match as distinct events.

crosswalk.match_basis: Identical date; epicenters ~0.15 lat apart (~17 km); magnitude identical (6.8), though reported as Ms (Ambraseys) vs MW (ISC) -- same numeric value across different scales is a coincidence worth noting, not proof of identical methodology.
Identical date; epicenters ~5 km apart; magnitude close (Ms7.2 vs Mw7.4). Numerous smaller ISC events (mb 4.5-5.2) the same day/next day nearby are aftershocks, NOT linked to this canonical_event_id.
crosswalk.note: 12 smaller same-day/next-day aftershocks (mb 4.46-5.16) found nearby, excluded from this match.

crosswalk.match_basis: Identical date; epicenters ~6 km apart (very close) -- essentially certain this is the same physical event (the 1999 Izmit/Kocaeli earthquake). HOWEVER the eq_historical.json record's own magnitude (mb 6.3, carried through as mw 6.3) is a well-known case of an early/preliminary real-time magnitude estimate that was never revised in this static snapshot -- the widely-accepted moment magnitude for this earthquake is Mw ~7.4-7.6 (e.g. USGS, Harvard CMT). Ambraseys' Ms7.4 is much closer to the accepted value than eq_historical.json's own mb6.3.
crosswalk.note: IMPORTANT: this is not a case of Ambraseys over- or under-estimating -- eq_historical.json itself under-represents this specific event's true size. Flagged so a future display policy does not treat eq_historical.json's value as the "authoritative" one by default.

crosswalk.match_basis: Identical date; epicenters ~0.6 km apart (essentially the same point) -- certain match (the 1999 Duzce earthquake). Same magnitude-underestimate pattern as Izmit above: eq_historical.json carries mb6.0/mw6.13 for this record, well below the widely-accepted Mw ~7.1-7.2 for this earthquake. Ambraseys' Ms7.1 matches the accepted value closely; eq_historical.json's own value does not.
crosswalk.note: Same magnitude-underestimate caveat as MARMARA-1999-08-17-IZMIT -- likely a systematic artifact of this particular EMSC static snapshot never being updated with the reviewed/CMT solution for either 1999 mainshock.
